## Background

![The reaction studied in this experiment: dissociation of the HCl dimer.](../images/ex01-reaction.jpeg){.reaction-fig fig-alt="(HCl)2 dissociates into two HCl molecules" width="420"}

There are many different "families" of basis sets [@jensen2013; @nagy2017], developed over the past sixty years by different computational chemists. Head-Gordon and co-workers [@witte2016] found that the most cost-effective basis sets for DFT belong to the Ahlrichs family [@weigend2005]. In this experiment you will analyze how they perform for the dissociation of the HCl dimer, taken from the NCCE30 subset [@peverati2014; @marshall2011; @vydrov2012; @lange2011; @mcmahon2011] of the Minnesota 2015B database [@yu2016a]. The reference energy for this dissociation is **2.01 kcal/mol**.

You will calculate the dissociation energy with three functionals, B3LYP [@vosko1980; @becke1988; @lee1988; @becke1993; @stephens1994], PBE [@perdew1996] and ωB97M-V [@vydrov2010; @mardirossian2016a], and with the Hartree–Fock (HF) method [@hartree1928; @hartree1928a; @fock1930; @slater1930]. You will use two families of basis sets:

- the **Ahlrichs** def2-SVP, def2-TZVP and def2-QZVP basis sets [@weigend2005];
- the **Dunning** correlation-consistent basis sets [@dunning1989; @woon1993; @woon1994; @wilson1999; @koput2002; @balabanov2005; @prascher2011], written cc-pV*n*Z, where "cc" means *correlation consistent* and *n* is D for double-ζ, T for triple-ζ or Q for quadruple-ζ.

For each method/basis combination, compute the reaction energy and its error with respect to the reference.

$$
\Delta E = 2\,E(\mathrm{HCl}) - E\big((\mathrm{HCl})_2\big)
$$

$$
\varepsilon = \Delta E_\text{comp} - \Delta E_\text{ref}
$$

::: {.callout-tip}
## Tip
When performing calculations, errors arise from different sources. Each basis set carries an error because it is a *truncated* expansion. This is the **basis set incompleteness error** (BSIE; computational chemists love acronyms). To minimize its impact, run calculations with the largest basis set you can afford. Put differently, you want the error from the basis set to be small, so that the error from the exchange–correlation functional is always the dominant one.
:::
